ile-de-france.name: Île-de-France
descriptions: Most populated region in France with 12 million inhabitants
Accounts for nearly 30% of national GDP
Includes Paris and 7 surrounding departments
Home to Versailles, Disneyland and La Défense
Connected by RER trains and 16 metro lines

normandie.name: Normandy
descriptions: Site of the Allied D-Day landings on June 6, 1944
Home of painter Claude Monet and his Water Lilies at Giverny
Famous for its camembert cheese and cider
Mont-Saint-Michel attracts 3 million visitors per year
Has 600 km of coastline on the English Channel

bretagne.name: Brittany
descriptions: Region where Breton, a Celtic language, is still spoken
Has 2,700 km of coastline, a third of France's shoreline
Home of crêpes, kouign-amann and salted butter caramel
Carnac has 3,000 standing stones aligned since prehistory
Its black and white flag is called the Gwenn ha Du

pays-de-la-loire.name: Pays de la Loire
descriptions: Crossed by the Loire, the longest river in France
Puy du Fou is one of Europe's most visited theme parks
Nantes hosts the famous Machines of the Isle with its giant elephant
The 24 Hours of Le Mans race has been held here yearly since 1923
Region known for its muscadet wines

centre.name: Centre-Val de Loire
descriptions: Home to over 300 castles along the Loire
Chambord is the largest Loire castle with 426 rooms
Joan of Arc liberated Orléans in 1429
Chartres Cathedral has 176 stained glass windows from the 12th century
Cereal region: known as the breadbasket of France

bourgogne.name: Bourgogne-Franche-Comté
descriptions: Region of grand Burgundy wines, listed as UNESCO heritage
Home of Dijon mustard and Comté cheese
The Dukes of Burgundy were as powerful as the kings of France
Mount Beuvray hosted Bibracte, a Gallic capital
Borders Switzerland to the east

grand-est.name: Grand Est
descriptions: Strasbourg hosts the European Parliament and Council of Europe
Home of champagne, produced only in this region
Famous for its Christmas markets, the oldest dating from 1570
Reims Cathedral crowned 33 kings of France
Borders 4 countries: Belgium, Luxembourg, Germany and Switzerland

hauts-de-france.name: Hauts-de-France
descriptions: Northernmost region of France
Connected to England by the Channel Tunnel
Site of the Battle of the Somme in 1916
The Arras belfry and other belfries are UNESCO-listed
Home of fries, maroilles cheese and bière de garde

auvergne.name: Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes
descriptions: Second most populated region in France
Mont Blanc, Europe's highest peak, reaches 4,808 m
Has 80 dormant volcanoes in the Chaîne des Puys
Lyon is the French capital of gastronomy
Home to the most visited ski resorts in the Alps worldwide

nouvelle-aquitaine.name: Nouvelle-Aquitaine
descriptions: Largest French region by area
Bordeaux is the world wine capital
Has Europe's tallest dune, the Dune of Pilat at 110 m
Lascaux Cave holds paintings 17,000 years old
Stretches from the Gironde estuary to the Pyrenees

occitanie.name: Occitanie
descriptions: Toulouse is the European capital of aeronautics with Airbus
The city of Carcassonne is Europe's largest fortified town
The Pont du Gard is a 2,000-year-old Roman aqueduct
The Canal du Midi has linked the Atlantic to the Mediterranean since 1681
The Millau Viaduct is the world's tallest bridge at 343 m

provence.name: Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur
descriptions: Marseille is France's oldest city, founded in 600 BC
The Côte d'Azur hosts the Cannes Film Festival every year
Region of lavender fields and olive oil
The Calanques form a national park between Marseille and Cassis
Avignon hosted 9 popes between 1309 and 1377

corse.name: Corsica
descriptions: Nicknamed the Island of Beauty, in the heart of the Mediterranean
Napoleon Bonaparte was born in Ajaccio in 1769
Has 1,000 km of coastline and many beaches
Monte Cinto peaks at 2,706 m, the highest point on the island
Corsican, a language close to Italian, is still spoken here

alsace.name: Alsace
descriptions: Historic northeastern region bordering Germany
Strasbourg hosts the European Parliament headquarters
Haut-Koenigsbourg Castle overlooks the Alsace plain
Home of kouglof, sauerkraut and Munster cheese
Features unique architecture with its timber-framed houses

guadeloupe.name: Guadeloupe
descriptions: Caribbean archipelago shaped like a butterfly
La Soufrière is an active volcano peaking at 1,467 m
Has 200,000 hectares of coral reefs
Birthplace of zouk music with the band Kassav'
Agricultural rum has been its specialty since the 17th century

martinique.name: Martinique
descriptions: Nicknamed the Island of Flowers for its vegetation
Mount Pelée destroyed Saint-Pierre in 1902
Birthplace of Empress Joséphine, wife of Napoleon
Produces an agricultural rum protected by AOC status
Has beaches of both black and white sand

guyane.name: French Guiana
descriptions: Only French territory in South America
Covered 95% by Amazon rainforest
The Guiana Space Centre has launched Ariane rockets since 1968
Home to over 700 bird species and 300,000 insects
Borders Brazil and Suriname

reunion.name: Réunion
descriptions: Volcanic island in the Indian Ocean, near Madagascar
Piton de la Fournaise erupts on average once a year
Three volcanic cirques are listed as UNESCO heritage
Birthplace of séga and maloya, two Creole music genres
Piton des Neiges peaks at 3,070 m

mayotte.name: Mayotte
descriptions: Small Indian Ocean island that became a French department in 2011
Has one of the world's largest enclosed lagoons
Shimaore and Kibushi are spoken alongside French
The maki, a small lemur, lives in the wild here
Youngest French department

polynesie.name: French Polynesia
descriptions: Made up of 118 islands scattered across the Pacific Ocean
Stretches over an area as large as Europe
Tahiti and Bora-Bora are the most famous islands
Painter Paul Gauguin lived and painted here at the end of his life
Has its own currency, the Pacific franc

nouvelle-caledonie.name: New Caledonia
descriptions: Southwest Pacific archipelago, near Australia
Has the world's second largest barrier reef
World's leading nickel producer after Indonesia
Home of the Kanak people, guardians of ancient traditions
Nicknamed the Pebble by its inhabitants

saint-pierre.name: Saint Pierre and Miquelon
descriptions: Small French archipelago off Canada, near Newfoundland
Has only 6,000 inhabitants spread across 8 islands
Only French territory in North America
During Prohibition, it was a major alcohol smuggling hub
Has its own time zone, 3 hours behind Paris

wallis.name: Wallis and Futuna
descriptions: Small French Pacific territory, near Fiji
Has 12,000 inhabitants on 2 main islands
Still ruled by 3 traditional customary kings
Wallisian and Futunan are spoken here
Most inhabitants are Catholic

saint-martin.name: Saint Martin
descriptions: Island shared between France and the Netherlands since 1648
Smallest island in the world divided between two countries
Sint Maarten airport is famous for planes skimming over the beach
Became a French overseas collectivity in 2007
Has 37 beaches and a tropical climate year-round
